text: No, this property was not deforested. The 67.7 ha of tree loss in 2020 was detected *before* the baseline period (2021–2025), meaning it occurred *prior* to 2021. The post-baseline assessment (2021–2025) found no further losses of 0.5 ha or more. While the property had some tree cover in 2000, JRC 2020 data confirms it was already classified as *non-forest* by 2020, so the 2020 loss did not meet the definition of deforestation (which requires loss of forest). The property had no forest to lose after 2020.
